messages:
Sam (PM): Quick sync — post-launch patch planning for prompt templates. We’ve got 12 bug reports where variables disappear in multi-line templates and 7 enhancement asks for the template library UX. Need to decide this week’s slice.
Priya (Eng): Can you paste the most common repro? I want to see if it’s a parsing edge or runtime cache issue.
Evan (Eng-ML): I saw a stack trace yesterday — looks like a KV cache eviction race when templates hit >1k token prefix.
Marta (SRE): Two customer incidents flagged as P1 (timeouts on bulk render). SLO impact: p50 unaffected, p95 spikes ~800ms for template-heavy calls.
Jon (Design): From UX side, the enhancement asks are mostly: saved templates library, variable autocomplete, and preview pane. Small wins but higher polish.
Sam (PM): Proposal: triage by (1) customer impact, (2) regression risk, (3) dev effort. If bugs cause SLO regressions we prioritize a hotfix; otherwise do a UX mini-ship in the same sprint. Thoughts?
Priya (Eng): Agree. Quick datapoint: of the 12 reports, 9 come from two large customers doing bulk exports. If we fix cache eviction it’ll cover most. Estimated: 3 dev-days + 1 day testing + canary.
Evan (Eng-ML): Patch suggestion: pin prefix-length in KV cache for template render paths and add a guard on eviction order. I can sketch a patch and perf test.
Priya (Eng): +1. Would like to land a small test that simulates 10k concurrent renders to validate.
Marta (SRE): Canary plan: route 10% of heavy-template traffic to a dedicated instance for 24h, monitor p95/p99 and error rate. If pass -> roll to 50% then 100%. I’ll write the runbook.
Sam (PM): OK — can we do bug hotfix + UX polish in parallel? Prioritize bug as release A, UX as release B scoped to smaller set (autocomplete + preview only).
Jon (Design): I’ll cut the scope: only variable autocomplete & preview pane for this sprint. Mockups done by EOD.
Evan (Eng-ML): Patch PR incoming tomorrow morning with tests.
Priya (Eng): I’ll pick up the cache guard and add the eviction test. Dev estimate: 4 days total between Evan+me.
Marta (SRE): I’ll own the canary and rollback hooks. Adding alarms: template-render latency > 600ms p95 or errors > 0.5% -> auto-fallback to previous model bundle.
Sam (PM): Great. Acceptance criteria for hotfix: replicable test that covers customer repro, p95 back to baseline in canary, no new errors in 24h. For UX: shipped autocomplete + preview behind feature flag, telemetry on usage.
Priya (Eng): Tagging @Jon for any UX questions during implementation.
Jon (Design): Got it — will add edge-case notes for multi-line variables.
rollouts-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-03-25 18:00 UTC -> 10% traffic to template-hotfix. (reacted :rocket:)
Sam (PM): Next steps: Evan + Priya pair on patch, Marta owned canary, Jon final mocks, Sam will update roadmap and customer comms. We’ll reconvene after canary results. :thumbsup:
Evan (Eng-ML): Quick log snippet for the repro attached here in thread — run:`
```
# repro script (short)
python -c "from templates import render; print(render(open('huge_template.txt').read(), vars={'x': 'y'*10000}))"
```
Priya (Eng): Nice. Will use that in the performance test.
Sam (PM): Thanks team — marking this as the sprint priority. I’ll update the ticket with acceptance criteria and assign owners.
